subject: SOC2 point-of-capture and roll-forward evidence timing
messages:
From: BrightLine Audit <audit@brightline-audit.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify point-of-capture for SOC 2 period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31)

Hi Jordan / team,

Quick question as we prepare Type II fieldwork: you stated the SOC 2 period is 2026-10-01 through 2027-03-31. To validate control evidence we need confirmation on the exact point-of-capture conventions you used for event logs and aggregated metrics. Specific items: 

- Are timestamps normalized to UTC for audit evidence, or do you preserve local-region timestamps in primary logs?
- For events that occur at the boundary day (2027-03-31), do your snapshots treat 2027-03-31 23:59:59 as in-scope, or is there any system processing that effectively rolls events into 2027-04-01 for reporting?
- For services that batch/aggregate (example: billing usage rollups), is there a documented delay window (e.g., up to 5 minutes after midnight) we should consider when selecting evidence samples?
- If there is a roll-forward / bridge approach for a migration or cutover on 2027-04-01, what formal statement will Redwood provide (bridge letter) and can you provide a draft during fieldwork?

Can you respond with the authoritative answers and attach a small sample of raw event logs around 2027-03-31 midnight (timezone annotated) so we can check capture behavior? If you have a bridge letter draft, please include.

Thanks,

Dana Park
Senior Auditor
BrightLine Audit

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify point-of-capture for SOC 2 period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31)

Marissa / Soojin — forwarding Dana's questions. Can you each take an ownerable piece: Marissa, please pull a redacted sample of the raw event logs spanning 2027-03-31 23:50:00 UTC through 2027-04-01 00:10:00 UTC and call out any aggregation delays; Soojin, please draft a short bridge letter statement we can sign if any roll-forward explanation is required (examples of cutover/maintenance windows are fine).

We should confirm whether our official evidence timestamps are stored in UTC and whether any internal processes cause late-arriving events to be reflected in daily aggregates for the prior day. I want a single consolidated reply back to Dana including attachments.

Jordan Blake
Director, Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify point-of-capture for SOC 2 period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31)

Jordan / Marissa — notes below and actions completed. Keeping this tight for audit.

Summary answers (authoritative):
- Timestamp convention: all production telemetry and raw event logs are ingested and stored in UTC. Surface-level UIs display local timezone but raw evidence is UTC.
- Point-of-capture for 2027-03-31: our canonical snapshot boundary is inclusive through 2027-03-31 23:59:59 UTC. That timestamp is the last in-scope instant.
- Aggregation delay: certain batch jobs (billing usage rollups, analytics aggregation) run in a 00:00–00:10 UTC window; aggregates may include events with ingestion timestamps within that window but we attach the original event timestamp (UTC) when reconciling.
- Roll-forward / bridge: we provide a signed bridge letter only when a known cutover/migration or documented exception occurred that materially affects the report period. If you require one for April 1 activities, we'll provide a short bridge letter certifying no control degradation and describing the minimal roll-forward handling.

Attached: draft bridge-letter-draft.pdf (template), log-sample-20270331.jsonl (redacted). The log sample includes three events spanning 2027-03-31 23:58:43 UTC through 2027-04-01 00:03:27 UTC; each entry includes the original event_timestamp field and the ingestion_timestamp field (both UTC). Note: a small minority (~0.4%) of events are late-arriving and appear in aggregates after midnight due to upstream retries; we can supply a reconciliation report on request.

Action items:
- Marissa: reconcile the redacted sample with the aggregate rollup for billing (please include the rollup job run timestamps).
- Jordan: I can produce the bridge letter text; sign-off needed.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge-letter-draft.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)
Attachment: log-sample-20270331.jsonl (JSONL, 32 KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <audit@brightline-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify point-of-capture for SOC 2 period (2026-10-01 to 2027-03-31)

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear questions. Confirming the authoritative responses below and attaching the requested artifacts.

Authoritative confirmations (official):
- Timestamps: All primary logs and telemetry are stored in UTC. We will provide redacted extracts showing event_timestamp and ingestion_timestamp in UTC.
- Boundary inclusivity: Our SOC 2 report period is inclusive through 2027-03-31 23:59:59 UTC; that instant is the last in-scope point.
- Aggregation behavior: Some background aggregation jobs run between 00:00 and 00:10 UTC; those aggregates reference original event timestamps. A small portion of events (<1%) can be late-arriving due to upstream retries, which may show in aggregates after midnight. We have included a short reconciliation summary in the log sample.
- Bridge letter: If you require a formal roll-forward statement for activities that occurred on 2027-04-01, attached is a draft bridge letter. The text states the scope of the roll-forward and that no control exceptions affecting the reporting period were identified. We will sign and return a final bridge letter if BrightLine requires it for your testing.

Attachments: bridge-letter-draft.pdf, log-sample-20270331.jsonl
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-EXAMPLE (supporting reconciliation), HubSpot record: BRG-2093

Let me know if you want the reconciliation in a different format or a short call to walk through the sample.

Best,
Jordan Blake
